module_title: Computer Abbreviations - Foundational Hardware & Everyday Tech
introduction: In the computer awareness section of competitive exams, full forms are guaranteed, high-scoring questions that require strict rote memorization. This foundational tier covers the most critical hardware components, memory types, and everyday tech acronyms.

core_concepts.title: Core Processing & Memory
core_concepts.description:
- CPU: Central Processing Unit
- ALU: Arithmetic Logic Unit
- CU: Control Unit
- RAM: Random Access Memory
- ROM: Read-Only Memory

core_concepts.title: System Booting
core_concepts.description:
- BIOS: Basic Input/Output System (The firmware used to perform hardware initialization during the booting process).
- CMOS: Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor (A battery-powered memory chip that stores startup info like system time and date).

core_concepts.title: Everyday Tech & Ports
core_concepts.description:
- USB: Universal Serial Bus
- PDF: Portable Document Format
- Wi-Fi: Wireless Fidelity
- OS: Operating System

important_entities.name: BIOS
important_entities.significance: This is one of the most frequently asked abbreviations. It is the very first software that runs when a computer is powered on.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will provide options like 'United Serial Bus' or 'Universal System Bus'. The exact rote memory must be locked onto **Universal Serial Bus**.
Many candidates think Wi-Fi stands for 'Wireless Fiber' or 'Wireless File'. It strictly stands for **Wireless Fidelity**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Focus on 'Metal-Oxide'. If you see 'Metal-Optical' or 'Memory-Oxide' in the options, instantly eliminate them.

exam_strategy_tips: For Tier-1 exams, memorize PDF as 'Portable Document Format', NOT 'Printed Document Format'. Examiners frequently use 'Printed' as a trap.
